articles.title: 'Emergency brake not working': Video captures moments leading to Assam train derailment
articles.description: A chilling video captures the moments before the Kolkata-Sairang Express derailed near Guwahati, with the driver heard reporting a red signal and a non-functional emergency system before the locomotive hits barricades with a loud thud. The locomotive and five coaches derailed at Digaru railway station on Wednesday morning. No injuries or casualties were reported.

articles.title: Stock market today: Sensex jumps over 1,000 points, Nifty50 adds 1% in opening trade
articles.full_text: Stock market today: Top reasons why stock market is rallying Nifty 50 has surged by 8.6% in just six trading days of this month. This surge was triggered mainly by the aggressive FII buying of Rs 53170 crores so far this month. The dramatic change in the market environment was triggered by positive global cues for India from the weakening of the AI trade. But it is important to note that the real fundamental support to the rally has come from the better-than-expected Q2 results. The near 24% earnings growth in Nifty 50 in Q2 is a 12-quarter high and has compressed the forward PE for Nifty 50 to fair levels. NSE Nifty50 advanced 319.65 points, or 1.28%, to 25,361.90 in early trade. IndiGo led early gainers on the index, rising Rs 225.60, or 4.15%, to Rs 5,655.60. Mahindra & Mahindra gained Rs 100.40, or 3.05%, to Rs 3,391, while Power Grid Corporation climbed Rs 5.30, or 2.05%, to Rs 263.25. State Bank of India advanced Rs 21, or 2.02%, to Rs 1,063, while Asian Paints rose Rs 47.70, or 1.90%, to Rs 2,557. Benchmark indices opened on a strong note on Wednesday, with BSE Sensex jumping 1,227.30 points, or 1.51%, to 82,333.95 in early trade. IndiGo led the gainers, rising 4.33% to Rs 5,648. Mahindra & Mahindra followed with a 3.53% gain to Rs 3,400.05, while Asian Paints advanced 2.45% to Rs 2,563.10. Bharti Airtel climbed 2.29% to Rs 2,112.20, SBI gained 2.10% to Rs 1,063.35 and HDFC Bank rose 1.98% to Rs 811.85. Benchmark indices are expected to open higher after the Diwali holiday break, supported by lower crude oil prices and strong foreign fund inflows. GIFT Nifty futures were trading at 25,334, indicating a positive start for the Nifty 50. The benchmark index had ended its previous trading session at 25,044.65, marking a closing high of more than eight months. Indian stock markets remained closed on Tuesday on account of Diwali. The positive opening indication came after the Nifty 50 and BSE Sensex gained nearly 9% during November. Easing crude prices, strong domestic earnings and renewed foreign portfolio investor interest have been among the factors supporting the recent rally in Indian equities. Asian equities showed a mixed but broadly positive trend, with Japan's Nikkei 225 climbing for a third consecutive session as data and earnings reports revived some optimism around the artificial intelligence sector. The benchmark advanced 0.80% to 60,942.48 at the midday break, while the broader Topix gained 0.79% to 3,924.51. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares also rose 0.2%, while South Korea's KOSPI gained 0.4%. China's blue-chip stocks, however, slipped 0.2%. The gains came against the backdrop of weakness on Wall Street, where US stocks had declined following hotter-than-anticipated inflation data. The mixed performance across Asian markets highlighted the differing trends in regional equities, with Japanese and South Korean benchmarks gaining while Chinese blue chips remained under pressure. Benchmarks extended their winning run after a sharp weekly rally, with buying in blue-chip banking and financial stocks and a correction in crude oil prices supporting the gains. BSE Sensex had surged 6,568.49 points, or 8.82%, in the previous week, while NSE Nifty advanced 1,977.25 points, or 8.57%. In the subsequent session on Monday, the 30-share Sensex climbed 107.25 points, or 0.13%, to settle at 81,106.65. It had touched an intraday high of 81,339.41, gaining 340.01 points, or 0.41%. The Nifty rose 58.25 points, or 0.23%, to close at 25,044.65. Among Sensex constituents, State Bank of India, Trent, Larsen & Toubro, NTPC, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank were among the leading gainers. HCL Tech, Tata Steel, UltraTech Cement and Bajaj Finance, however, featured among the major laggards. Meanwhile, Brent crude declined 1.04% to $97.46 per barrel.

articles.title: ‘De-risk, not decouple’: Bessent says US-China must cooperate on AI risks
articles.description: The United States and China plan to initiate a dialogue on superintelligence risks during an upcoming meeting. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent highlighted the importance of cooperation in managing artificial intelligence risks. The discussion aims to address shared technological challenges and ensure human oversight remains paramount. Trade agreements have also been outlined to strengthen economic ties between the two nations.

articles.title: NCERT conducts five-day NISHTHA training for Delhi teachers, focuses on NEP 2020, new textbooks and classroom reforms
articles.description: The NCERT and SCERT Delhi conducted a five-day teacher training programme under the Reimagined NISHTHA initiative from November 2 to 6, 2026.
